title: When the caller is an AI agent: how insurers should prepare
summary: Personal AI agents are starting to contact insurers. Here's why insurance is harder than retail, and how carriers should recognize, verify and serve them.
body_markdown:
## Our approach: detect, verify, route, control, log


Strada is built for insurance from the ground up. Our AI agents already handle claims and servicing work for carriers, MGAs and TPAs across voice, chat, email and SMS. They work inside the policy, claims and billing systems those operations run on, follow rules each client sets, and hand off to people with full context when judgment is needed. That matters for agent traffic. Recognizing that a caller is software is the easy part. The hard part is acting correctly on a real policy or claim, with insurance-specific controls, and that is where Strada already operates.


Our approach to agent traffic builds on that foundation and follows the order in which an interaction unfolds.


**Detect.** The first step is to assess whether the other party is a person or an agent, across voice, chat and email. Some agents identify themselves and many do not, so detection should not depend on the agent announcing itself. When an agent is recognized, the interaction can move to a path designed for it.


**Verify.** Detection says what the caller is. Verification establishes whom it acts for and what it is allowed to do, and it should not depend on detection: a capable agent can sound like a person, so sensitive actions need the same checks whoever is on the line. Answers to knowledge-based questions are not proof of delegation on their own. Before anything sensitive, the policyholder confirms the request through a channel already on file, such as a text or email to the contact details the carrier holds. Where a protocol supports it, a delegated sign-in that the policyholder granted directly can take the place of that step.


**Route to agent workflows.** An agent does not need small talk, empathy statements or a menu read aloud. It needs precise, structured and complete answers, with the relevant conditions and disclosures attached so that what reaches the policyholder is accurate. Agent workflows should also handle requests that a person would never make in one call, such as a provider checking the status of many claims at once. When a request needs judgment, the workflow hands off to a person with the full context of what the agent asked and what was already shared.


**Control.** Each carrier, MGA or TPA sets its own rules for agent traffic, action by action. As an illustration, a carrier might let a verified agent check claim status or request documents directly, require the policyholder's confirmation to change a payment method, add a driver or cancel a policy, and send coverage disputes or injury claims to a licensed adjuster. The rules can differ for personal agents and for business agents, and should apply the same way on every channel.


**Log.** Every agent interaction should be recorded: who the agent said it acted for, how that was verified, what it asked, what it received and which rule applied. That record supports the carrier's AI governance program and gives a clear answer if a policyholder later disputes what their agent did.


These principles hold regardless of how the agent arrives. Today that is mostly the phone, the web and email. As carriers adopt structured standards such as agent-to-agent protocols, MCP, or the Personal Agent Protocol, the same verification, rules and audit trail should carry over to those connections, and Strada will universally support them.
